St. Titus of Crete

Saints

St. Titus of Crete

Period
First century
Region
Eastern Mediterranean
Titles / vocation
Apostle · Hierarch · Missionary
Commemoration
August 25

Introduction

St. Titus is Paul’s fellow worker and the bishop of Crete remembered by the OCA among the Seventy.

Read the published life [1]

BackgroundLife and notable eventsDeath and martyrdomWritings and legacyChronology
Death / martyrdom

Peaceful death in old age, according to the life.

Read circumstances and sources

Background

The Orthodox life describes a Cretan upbringing in pagan learning and a turn toward the Hebrew prophets before his Christian mission.

[1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 1; Published biographical account,paragraph 2; Published biographical account,paragraph 3

Paul, a servant of God, and an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of God’s elect, and the acknowledging of the truth which is after godliness;

In hope of eternal life, which God, that cannot lie, promised before the world began;

But hath in due times manifested his word through preaching, which is committed unto me according to the commandment of God our Saviour;

To Titus, mine own son after the common faith: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ our Saviour.

For this cause left I thee in Crete, that thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city, as I had appointed thee:

If any be blameless, the husband of one wife, having faithful children not accused of riot or unruly.

For a bishop must be blameless, as the steward of God; not selfwilled, not soon angry, not given to wine, no striker, not given to filthy lucre;

But a lover of hospitality, a lover of good men, sober, just, holy, temperate;

Holding fast the faithful word as he hath been taught, that he may be able by sound doctrine both to exhort and to convince the gainsayers.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · Titus 1: 1–9

Life and notable events

The canonical letters show Paul entrusting him with work in Corinth and the ordering of churches in Crete; the later life adds missionary miracles.

[1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 3; Published biographical account,paragraph 5; Published biographical account,paragraph 6 · [2] Public-domain Bible translation · Titus 1:4–9 (KJV); 2Cor 8:16–24 (KJV)

But thanks be to God, which put the same earnest care into the heart of Titus for you.

For indeed he accepted the exhortation; but being more forward, of his own accord he went unto you.

And we have sent with him the brother, whose praise is in the gospel throughout all the churches;

And not that only, but who was also chosen of the churches to travel with us with this grace, which is administered by us to the glory of the same Lord, and declaration of your ready mind:

Avoiding this, that no man should blame us in this abundance which is administered by us:

Providing for honest things, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men.

And we have sent with them our brother, whom we have oftentimes proved diligent in many things, but now much more diligent, upon the great confidence which I have in you.

Whether any do enquire of Titus, he is my partner and fellowhelper concerning you: or our brethren be enquired of, they are the messengers of the churches, and the glory of Christ.

Wherefore shew ye to them, and before the churches, the proof of your love, and of our boasting on your behalf.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · 2 Corinthians 8: 16–24

Death and martyrdom

The life describes peaceful death at 97. That age and death account are presented here as the later Orthodox tradition.

[1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 10

Writings and legacy

The epistle addressed to St. Titus and Paul’s accounts of his fellow worker preserve direct biblical testimony alongside the later Orthodox life.

[1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 6; Published biographical account,paragraph 7

When I shall send Artemas unto thee, or Tychicus, be diligent to come unto me to Nicopolis: for I have determined there to winter.

Bring Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their journey diligently, that nothing be wanting unto them.

And let ours also learn to maintain good works for necessary uses, that they be not unfruitful.

All that are with me salute thee. Greet them that love us in the faith. Grace be with you all. Amen.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · Titus 3: 12–15

Chronology

  1. Apostolic ministry

    Paul calls St. Titus his fellow worker.

    [1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 7; Published biographical account,paragraph 10

  2. Mission in Crete

    Paul entrusts him with ordering the churches.

    [1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 5; Published biographical account,paragraph 7

  3. End of life

    The Orthodox account describes peaceful repose.

    [1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 10
